88 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

THE COLLEGE PUBLICATION

ORIGIN AND EXTENT—Frequent reference has been made in this study to The Platonian Messenger. This paper was a combined newspaper and literary magazine, sponsored, as the name suggests, by the Platonian Literary Society, and published monthly during the collegiate year. It was edited at Savoy by the professors and submitted students and published monthly during the collegiate year. It was edited at Savoy by the professors and contributed by the student body. From the earliest issues to the last one available, it appears to have been an effective publication, 1886-1887, the last issue available being that of November, 1886. How much longer it ran is a matter of conjecture; but the fact that the 1887-1888 catalog makes no mention of it seems to indicate that by that date it had ceased to exist by that time.

THE FORMAT—The paper was printed by the Bonham press, and distributed in sheet form. The paper was folded to make a folder of eight four-column pages eleven inches by about eight or nine inches. The front page appeared as a four-page, five-column single-fold paper measuring thirteen inches by about twenty inches. The paper was printed for the most part in 12-point standard-weight type, with poetry and other items set in larger type.
